Previously they would issue a notice for more evidence or intent to deny and give the applicant a change to respond before proceeding with a decision. Show less Read more Like 20 Dislike Reply @chuckholmes561 7 months ago The purpose of this video interview with a lawyer is not to clarify, it is to scare you so that you pay thousands of dollars to an immigration attorney to handle your case. The law did not change, USCIS is simply emphasizing the need for evidence of a relationship if you came here on a visitor visa and got married to prove that you did not commit fraud. If you came here on a visa, you got married to an American and have a real relationship with them, nothing to worry about, your application is going to be approved, whether you have a lawyer or not. Just have your sponsor file all the paperwork and pay the fees according to the instructions.
